title: Successful exFAT ftruncate retains the old logical size
mechanism: The public ExfatInode::resize used by ftruncate delegates to ExfatInodeInner::resize, which only updates size_allocated and clusters (size is assigned only when clusters decrease below the old size), and never publishes the logical size itself, so extension and same-cluster shrink leave inner.size unchanged.
contract: ftruncate(2): on success the file length becomes exactly the requested size. Extension reads as zeros and data beyond a shrink is lost.
observed: ftruncate(fd, 1) and ftruncate(fd, 8192) on an empty exFAT file returned 0 with st_size 0, and ftruncate(fd, 2048) on a 4096-byte file returned 0 with st_size 4096 and all 4096 bytes still readable.

repro.how_to_run: Run the script on a host with QEMU/KVM, mkfs.ext2, mkfs.exfat and a static C toolchain after pointing QEMU, MKFS_EXFAT, GLIBC_STATIC and KERNEL at local paths. MC4BUG lines and MC4VERDICT BUG mean the bug fired.
